answer: A registry should require each agent to forge a stake-backed identity by locking a refundable deposit before it can trade. A falcon-style audit then samples a random slice of new identities each epoch and demands a fresh proof of useful work; an identity that fails the audit forfeits its deposit. Honest agents pay once and trade freely, while a sybil farmer must fund every echo of itself at full cost, so each extra clone costs real money and yields no extra voting weight.
